title: The Most Misunderstood Concept in Physics
subject: Physics
beats: Teases a concept that governs storms, the universe and maybe time itself
Asks strangers what Earth gets from the sun; most say energy
Asks how much energy Earth radiates back; most guess less because we use it
Reveals it is the same amount; so what are we really getting?
Jumps to 1813: young Sadi Carnot, Napoleon, Paris falls
Carnot's father, steam engines, French designs behind Britain's
Engines convert only about 3%; Carnot studies the ideal engine
Hot bar, cold bar, chamber, piston, flywheel: walks the cycle step by step
Runs the ideal engine in reverse; everything returns to the start
You'd expect a reversible engine to be 100% efficient; it isn't
Hot gas pushes harder than cold gas, so some heat must be dumped
To raise efficiency, heat the hot side or cool the cold side
Kelvin imagines gas so cold the particles stop: absolute zero
Replaces heat with temperatures; efficiency formula on screen
Efficiency depends only on temperatures; 100% is impossible
Real engines: 32% theoretical vs 3% actual; heat leaks into walls and axle
Spread-out energy can't be recovered: same energy, less usable
Clausius names the measure of spreading: entropy
The first two laws: energy is constant, entropy tends to a maximum
Why hot things cool, gas fills containers, no perpetual motion
Entropy is usually called disorder; better: energy's tendency to spread
Physics laws run both ways in time, so where does the direction come from?
Toy model: 8 atoms per bar, 7 and 3 energy packets hopping randomly
Snapshot: 9 packets left, 1 right; heat went cold to hot!
Boltzmann: not impossible, just improbable; counts configurations
10.5% chance at small scale; 0.05% at 80 atoms; never at real scale
Rubik's cube: one solved state, quintillions of messy ones
Then how does air conditioning push heat from cold to hot?
Only by raising entropy more at the power plant
If entropy always rises, how does any structure or life exist?
Earth isn't closed: the sun gives a stream of low entropy
Plants, animals, predators: each step spreads energy more
Back to interviewees: same energy out; one photon in, 20 out
Speculative: life may be a consequence of the second law (England)
Where did the sun get its low entropy? Back to the Big Bang
The past hypothesis says it was low, not why
But the early universe was uniform; how was that low entropy?
Gravity flips it: spread-out matter is the unlikely state
Entropy budgets: stars, gas, neutrinos, CMB
Bekenstein, Hawking: black holes have entropy and a temperature
Black holes hold almost all the universe's entropy
Low-to-high entropy is the arrow of time
Heat death: the arrow of time disappears
Tea and milk: complexity lives in the middle, where we are
